description: I'm joining the NASA Space Apps Challenge as a solo participant this year. I’m planning to work on a project that utilizes NASA's open data to fulfill the requirements of the "Space Mission Design Game" challenge. I'm looking forward to learning, experimenting, and building a useful tool over the course of the hackathon.
summary:
Spaceflight Director is an immersive, physics-driven orbital mechanics and space science simulation built in Godot Engine using C#.

What we developed: A fully interactive space flight simulator where users take complete command of a space program, handling rocket ascent, real-time trajectory tracking, resource management, and scientific data collection.

How it addresses the challenge: It translates complex aerospace principles—including N-body gravity, Keplerian orbits, the Tsiolkovsky rocket equation into an engaging, self-contained simulation. Players must actively manage electric charge, fuel reserves, and execute precise orbital maneuvers.

Why it is important: It bridges the gap between advanced aerospace engineering and accessible education. By providing a hands-on, offline-capable environment to visualize orbital dynamics, it inspires and empowers students and space enthusiasts to interact directly with real-world space science concepts.
details:
Project Overview: Spaceflight Director (v0.2.0.0)

Spaceflight Director is an immersive, physics-driven space science and flight simulation built for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026. It puts players directly in command of an active space program, challenging them to manage electric power, execute precise orbital maneuvers, and conduct real-world scientific observations around Earth.

What It Does and How It Works

Spaceflight Director models real-world aerospace engineering and orbital mechanics through a playable simulation loop:

  • Ascent and Orbital Insertion: Players launch rockets using custom SAS autopilot modes (Prograde and Retrograde) to achieve a stable orbit.
  • Flight Operations and Mechanics: The game relies on authentic mathematical models, including N-Body gravity, Keplerian orbits, patched conics, and the Tsiolkovsky Rocket Equation to calculate mass, fuel consumption, and delta-v constraints.
  • Resource Management: Onboard avionics and SAS autopilots continuously consume electric charge, forcing players to carefully monitor power drain.
  • Time-Warping: A custom time-warp engine safely accelerates simulation speeds up to thousands of times normal speed, allowing players to bypass long orbital transit phases without breaking physics calculations.
  • Scientific Observation: Players collect telemetry and data using onboard science instruments during orbital operations.

Tech Stack and Architecture

The project was developed using modern, high-performance game development tools:

  • Engine: Godot Engine 4.x (.NET Edition)
  • Programming Language: C# (.NET 8.0)
  • Physics and Mathematics: Custom procedural numerical physics integration (100% self-contained for optimized offline performance).
  • Target Platform: Windows Executable (.exe)

Creativity and Design Choices

  • Bridging Simulation and Playability: Translating complex astrodynamics into an interactive experience is a major creative achievement. Instead of purely abstract data entry, my team built a custom real-time trajectory line renderer and intuitive UI dashboards.
  • Seamless Time Manipulation: Space travel involves massive distances and long coast periods. Implementing a custom time-warp engine that safely compresses time while preserving mathematical integrity solves a classic problem in space sims.
  • Focused Systems: By tying core controls (WASD rotational inputs, staging, SAS toggles) directly to realistic constraints like electric power drain and rocket staging, the game creates meaningful decision-making loops for the player.

Factors Considered by the Team

  • Mathematical Accuracy vs. Accessibility: The team balanced strict real-world aerospace math (like the Tsiolkovsky rocket equation and orbital state propagation) with features like SAS autopilots to ensure the game remains challenging yet fun to pilot.
  • Performance and Portability: Designing self-contained numerical solvers and leveraging Godot's lightweight .NET environment ensured the simulation runs smoothly offline without heavy external dependencies.
  • Mission Flow: Designing a clear gameplay loop—from launch ascent to orbital insertion, resource monitoring, and scientific data collection—provides players with a satisfying progression structure.
